meta.question: Which database should the new order service use?
meta.title: Choosing a database for the order service
meta.author: Architecture group

answer.headline: Use PostgreSQL: orders need multi-row transactions and ad-hoc reporting, and our load is well within what one managed primary with read replicas can serve.
answer.text: DynamoDB scales further but pushes joins and reporting into application code; MongoDB fits flexible documents, which orders are not. Revisit if sustained writes pass about 5,000 per second.
points: Transactions across orders, lines and payments come built in
The team already runs PostgreSQL in production
Reporting queries work without a separate data pipeline

options.name: PostgreSQL
pros: SQL for reporting and support queries
Skills and tooling already in house
options.verdict: Best fit for the next three years.

options.name: DynamoDB
cons: Access patterns must be designed up front

options.name: MongoDB
options.verdict: Solves a problem we do not have.

blocks.title: p99 write latency in our load test
From the design review
blocks.text: Every order question support asks us is a join. Pick the database that answers joins.

blocks.title: Where the database sits
blocks.caption: Step through the order flow to see where order data is written. The ledger store on the right is the database this decision covers.

blocks.title: When to revisit
blocks.label: Review trigger
blocks.body: Re-open this decision if sustained writes pass **5,000 per second**, or if a single table grows beyond about 2 TB. Both are at least two years away on current growth.
